title: Video Editor and Motion Designer, Temporary
description:

Since then, the team has amassed nearly 65 million views. Now we’re building out the second phase of our social video strategy and have launched a new YouTube team dedicated to producing midlength adaptations for the platform.

We are looking for a video editor and motion designer who has a passion for accountability journalism and is excited by the opportunity to bring our reporting to an increasing number of viewers who treat YouTube as a platform to learn about the world around them.

You should be comfortable working with reporters and editors across the newsroom as well as freelancers we’ll bring on to help with projects.

This is a temporary two-year role that will report to our director of multiplatform audience strategy. The YouTube team sits within the larger ProPublica audience team.

  • Collaborate with producers to create videos — and related promo cuts — that are grounded in ethical journalistic principles, standards and practices.

  • Communicate proactively with the team regarding project status and timelines and directly collaborate with producers on scoping and delivering videos on schedule. 
  • Manage multiple projects in various stages of production, sometimes meeting tight deadlines.

We are looking for candidates who have proven that they can use video editing and design skills for journalistic ends.

  • Four or more years of professional video editing and motion design experience in a newsroom, media organization or production studio. 
  • High proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, with expert proficiency in both Adobe After Effects and Premiere Pro.
  • A portfolio that highlights videos you have edited specifically for YouTube, including hosted, vlog-style and/or explainer formats.
  • Experience building tension in hooks, controlling pacing and navigating tonal shifts in video storytelling. 
  • You are energized by the opportunity of being part of a founding team and creating something from scratch — establishing formats, defining visual languages and building efficient workflows. 
  • You thrive while collaborating, seeking input from others and iterating your work based on feedback. 

And many of these: 

  • Experience being part of a founding YouTube team or launching a new project initiative. 
  • Experience in on-site production, including shooting on professional camera equipment and knowledge of lighting and audio setups.
  • Experience with digital asset management and video archival workflows.

The Role

Our AI Platform team builds the technology that powers AI-enabled products and services, for internal users and external customers. We design, build and operate the infrastructure, patterns and reusable capabilities that enable generative and agentic AI, natural language processing, predictive analytics and machine learning across the Group, from customer-facing features in our digital products to the internal tools used by colleagues across our four businesses.

Scope

We are seeking an Engineering Manager to lead our Applied AI and Data Science team: a multidisciplinary group of AI Engineers, ML Engineers, NLP Engineers and Data Scientists. This is a player-coach role. You will own the health, delivery and growth of the team while remaining a hands-on contributor to its work, writing and reviewing code, shaping architecture and stepping into implementation when it matters.

The team’s work spans generative and agentic AI systems built on large language models, alongside the NLP and predictive models that sit behind our products and internal tools. You will turn the Group’s AI ambitions into well-architected, production-grade systems, working in close partnership with the Head of AI and Data Engineering, product managers, data engineers and business stakeholders to decide what we build, why we build it, and how we know it is working. You will also champion the team’s move to AI-native engineering, with coding agents used across the whole software development lifecycle.

Accountabilities

  • Lead and manage the team. Provide day-to-day management, mentorship and career development, and build one team across engineering and data science disciplines.
  • Own delivery. Own planning, resourcing, prioritisation and delivery with product management, balancing exploratory work against production commitments.
  • Communicate progress. Keep leadership and stakeholders informed on progress, risks and trade-offs, and set realistic expectations of what AI can deliver.
  • Stay hands on. Contribute directly to the team’s deliverables: build, prototype, review code and models, and step into implementation when it matters.
  • Contribute to technical and architectural decisions. Shape the architecture of our agentic AI, RAG, NLP and ML systems, covering agent design, model selection and build-versus-buy.
  • Oversee the development of safe and reliable agents. Ensure our agents have well-scoped tool permissions, guardrails and human-in-the-loop controls, and are evaluated end to end before and after release.
  • Ensure quality, security and compliance. Set standards for code quality, testing, evaluation, observability and cost, and keep AI systems secure, well-architected and compliant.
  • Champion AI-native engineering. Embed AI coding agents across the SDLC of the team, from specification and design to code, tests and review, with clear standards for AI-generated code.
  • Partner with others. Work with Product, Data Engineering, Security, Legal and the business units, challenging requirements and using metrics to define what “done” looks like.
  • Hire and grow the team. Recruit, interview and onboard engineers and data scientists, shaping the team’s skills mix to match the AI roadmap.
  • Drive best practices and ways of working. Improve CI/CD, experiment tracking and the path to production, and promote the team’s capabilities across the Group.

Selection criteria

Essential

  • A track record as an engineering manager or tech lead with direct people-management responsibility for AI/ML engineers, NLP engineers and/or data scientists.
  • Experience balancing hands-on technical contribution with people leadership and delivery ownership.
  • Strong hands-on AI/ML engineering background, with extensive Python experience and confidence reviewing code across LLM, agentic, NLP and classical ML systems.
  • Hands-on experience with modern agent frameworks such as Strands Agents, LangGraph or the Claude Agent SDK, and with interoperability standards such as MCP and A2A.
  • Strong cloud-native expertise on AWS, especially Amazon Bedrock and Bedrock AgentCore, alongside SageMaker, Lambda and Step Functions, with CDK or equivalent IaC.
  • Hands-on LLMOps and MLOps experience, including agent and trajectory evaluation, tracing (e.g. OpenTelemetry), guardrails, cost monitoring and automated model pipelines.
  • A clear understanding of agent security risks, such as prompt injection, data leakage and over-permissioned tools, and how to mitigate them.
  • Day-to-day experience of AI-native software delivery, using coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or GitHub Copilot across planning, coding, testing and review.
  • Able to set team standards for AI-assisted development, including context engineering for coding agents, review of AI-generated code and measuring its impact on delivery.
  • A solid grounding in applied data sci

The Economist Group is a global media and information services company committed to championing progress. We equip individuals and organisations with expertise, insights, and perspectives to navigate change and drive growth.

This is a full-time role at the centre of our new AI Lab, a small team exploring how generative AI might shape the future of Economist journalism. This role will focus on building and fine-tuning LLM-powered systems with a particular focus on editorial tone, style transfer, retrieval workflows, and multimodal generation (especially audio).

You’ll ship products from zero-to-one and see your ideas directly influence how millions of readers interact with our journalism.   • Fine-tune large language models (LLMs) for style and tone alignment with The Economist’s editorial voice
  • Design, curate, and manage datasets used for fine-tuning, including versioning and annotation workflows
  • Build and evaluate RAG pipelines that incorporate retrieval from structured content
  • Prototype and test TTS (text-to-speech) pipelines for use in audio-first products (leveraging tools like ElevenLabs, OpenAI TTS etc)
  • Collaborate with infra, frontend, and design leads to ship internal tools and demos that explore GenAI capabilities
  • Own quality evaluation pipelines (BLEU, ROUGE, editorial scoring, custom evals), including human-in-the-loop feedback loops
  • Support product experiments where real-time generation, summarisation, or personalization are being tested
  • Partner directly with journalists and editors to develop novel evaluation metrics that capture the nuances of The Economist's tone and style

  • Strong Python skills, including working with LangChain, HuggingFace Transformers, and data pipelines (Pandas, DVC, Weights & Biases)
  • Comfortable defining and tracking generation quality with eval metrics like BLEU, ROUGE, and building editorial-specific evaluators
  • Exposure to STT / TTS tools for prototyping (e.g., Whisper, ElevenLabs, Bark, etc.)
  • Strong communication and collaboration mindset — able to work closely with editorial and product stakeholders
  • Curious and exploratory — comfortable working in ambiguity and pushing the boundaries of GenAI capabilities

Strong Candidates Might Also Have

  • Experience fine-tuning models for style or persona (e.g. chatbots with specific character voices)
  • Exposure to LangSmith or similar observability tools for prompt / LLM testing
  • Knowledge of voice synthesis, cloning, or emotion conditioning in audio pipelines
  • Previous work in media, journalism, podcasting, or content production contexts
  • Familiarity with multi-modal generation (text + image + audio), or interest in pushing toward that frontier
  • Contributions to open-source LLM tools or libraries
  • An interest in the ethical, editorial, and philosophical questions raised by AI-generated content

We believe AI will fundamentally change both our business and the world around us, making our mission more vital than ever. While we already use AI across The Economist Group, we think the changes to come in the next few years could be even more far-reaching.

This is why we are launching the Economist AI Lab - to reimagine Economist journalism for an AI-driven world. It is a deliberately ambitious project, exploring new ideas and possibilities beyond our existing AI initiatives and engineering roadmap.

title: Asia Editor

Who we are

Semafor is a global news platform for an increasingly complex world in which consumers are overwhelmed by too many news sources and unsure what to trust. We are building Semafor to enable world-class journalists to deliver reporting and insights with rigor in journalistic forms that ensure a new level of transparency. Our editors and reporters distill the most important stories from all over in formats that uncover the forces shaping the stories, explain the interests behind polarizing narratives, and replenish the stock of shared facts. As a global platform, Semafor recognizes that smart people can disagree and that informed readers need to understand alternative points of view from competing centers of power and culture in a multi-polar world. Want to join us? Read on. 

About the Role

Semafor is expanding across Asia to help decision-makers in the region and around the world make sense of the region’s rapidly shifting dynamics in trade, technology, finance, geopolitics and global power, in the primary theater where the new global economy is being built. 

We want to connect the dots across this complex landscape, delivering rigorous, independent business journalism to the world’s most discerning readers and are looking for a talented journalist with deep knowledge of China and the Asia-Pacific region to help lead an expansion effort across digital platforms and live journalism. 

A seasoned leader with a track record of managing teams, the successful candidate will bring a deep understanding of the economic and financial forces transforming Asia — with a focus on how China is reshaping the region and the world. 

We’re looking for someone with an entrepreneurial attitude, a deep sense of their audience, sure feet and a clear voice to produce useful, revelatory, and fair coverage in an enormous and complex part of the world. This person will be charged with chronicling the forces shaping Asia including trade, technology, capital flows, energy, CEOs, power, politics, and policy.

The successful candidate will be well-sourced and eager to get scoops and deliver big interviews, while bringing a sophisticated perspective in delivering thought-provoking and insightful stories. Reporting to the Global Managing Editor, the Asia Editor will be charged with building out our Asia-based reporting team and products, targeting sophisticated, engaged, and globally aware readers who live in — or have deep interest and connections to — the region.

The ideal candidate will be based in Singapore, but Semafor is open to applicants in other parts of the region. 

Your responsibilities

  • Work with Semafor’s leaders to shape our Asia vision and product.
  • Help recruit for and build Semafor’s Asia-based reporting team.
  • Lead the development of Semafor’s Asia briefings and products that best cater to our readers, viewers, and listeners.
  • Anchor Semafor’s coverage across Asia — across all platforms and live journalism.
  • Write must-read stories about the region, with a focus on business, economics, technology, and energy for a sophisticated audience who live in, or have interest and connections to Asia.
  • Participate in event moderation, as well as media appearances on TV, radio, and podcasts.
  • Collaborate closely with other parts of Semafor’s global newsroom and audience teams.

 

What makes you qualified

  • 10+ years of journalism experience, including relevant experience covering Asia
  • A track record of newsroom leadership.
  • Experience and interest in global financial and business journalism.
  • A strategic, sophisticated approach to identifying themes and focuses of coverage across sectors and borders.
  • Bring speedy insight to big news stories, and flair and personality to writing.
  • A passion for world events and issues and a broad interest in a wide range of subjects.
  • Broad media consumption habits across conventional and unconventional sources.

  • Experience working with diverse teams with teammates from many different backgrounds.
  • Diligence and reliability to work without hands-on supervision.

title: Software Engineer
description:
1 big thing: Axios is a growth-focused media company dedicated to helping people get smarter, faster, on what matters. We’re looking for a Full Stack Software Engineer who pairs strong product-engineering fundamentals with modern AI-native development practices to build and scale the systems and experiences that power Axios’ core products.

Why it matters: At Axios, we deliver clear, trustworthy, and informative news to millions of readers every day. As a Full Stack Software Engineer, you’ll build the interfaces, services, APIs, and data flows behind our audience-facing products and publishing tools. 

AI has become a core part of how we build software. You’ll use coding agents and other AI tools throughout the development lifecycle—from understanding problems and exploring solutions through implementation, testing, review, debugging, documentation, and operation. You’ll remain accountable for the architecture, quality, security, and product outcomes of everything you ship.

You’ll work with product managers, designers, and engineers across disciplines to build resilient systems that embody Axios’ commitment to clarity and make our readers smarter.

Responsibilities:

As a Full Stack Software Engineer, you’ll deliver high-quality, reliable product features across Axios’ frontend and backend systems, using modern agentic development practices to accelerate delivery and ensuring performance and stability across our publishing and delivery platforms. Key responsibilities include:

  • End-to-end feature development: Own features across the frontend, APIs, business logic, data layer, testing, and production systems. Turn product problems into clear technical plans and reviewable units of work, using AI agents thoughtfully across research, prototyping, implementation, testing, refactoring, and documentation.
  • Frontend development: Create accessible, responsive, and maintainable interfaces using JavaScript or TypeScript, React, and modern web frameworks such as Next.js.
  • Backend and API development: Build production services and APIs that support Axios’ products and publishing workflows, and create clear contracts that can be understood and used reliably by people, applications, and AI-powered tools.
  • AI-enabled product development: Identify opportunities where models, agents, retrieval, or intelligent automation can create meaningful value for readers or internal teams. Build those capabilities with clear user controls, measurable behavior, appropriate guardrails, and an understanding of when conventional software is the better solution.
  • Quality and reliability: Write automated tests, improve performance, and contribute to logging, metrics, tracing, security, and operational reliability.
  • Collaboration: Partner with product, design, quality engineering, and other developers to clarify requirements, explain tradeoffs, and deliver effectively. Participate in code reviews, pairing, onboarding, and mentorship.
  • Product and technical improvement: Understand how technical work supports readers, editorial workflows, and business goals.Improve existing systems through thoughtful refactoring, sound technical decisions, and practical experimentation with emerging engineering approaches.

Skills:

The ideal candidate is a thoughtful engineer who cares about user experience, reliability, scalability, and maintainable code—and who has moved beyond occasional AI assistance to using agents as a substantive part of their engineering practice. You should have:

  • Experience: 2-5+ years of professional software development experience, with production experience in frontend, backend, or full-stack development and the ability to contribute across the stack.
  • AI-native development: Hands-on experience using agentic coding tools—such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or comparable tools—to complete meaningful, multi-step software work, rather than only generating snippets or using autocomplete.
  • Agent direction and context: Ability to write clear specifications and acceptance criteria, provide relevant context, break work into appropriately scoped tasks, decide what to delegate, and guide an agent when its initial approach is incomplete or incorrect.
  • Verification and engineering judgment: Ability to review AI-generated code critically, validate assumptions against the actual system, identify security and maintainability risks, and recognize when an agent-produced solution is plausible but wrong. You understand that AI increases the importance of sound architecture, testing, and human judgment.
  • Frontend development: Experience building production interfaces with JavaScript or TypeScript and React, preferably with Next.js or a comparable modern framework.
  • Backend development: Experience building production services and APIs. Our backend systems primarily use Go and Python, and you should be comfortable working in or learning either language.
  • Data fundamentals: Experience with relational databases, SQL, schema design, transactions, and migrations.
  • Quality and security: Experience with unit and integration testing, accessibility, input validation, authentication, authorization, and common web security practices.

description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest.

We are seeking a deputy research editor to help lead and strengthen ProPublica’s research team, guiding high-impact investigative work across the newsroom while supporting rigorous, collaborative and responsive research at scale.

The research team plays a critical role in many of ProPublica’s most impactful and widely read stories, contributing deep reporting, verification and sourcing to both long-term investigations and fast-turn accountability journalism. Research reporters regularly earn co-bylines and contributor credits across text, audio and video projects, and they collaborate closely with reporters, editors and partner newsrooms across the country.

The team works at scale and with flexibility, often supporting multiple major investigations while responding to urgent, high-priority requests tied to breaking news. This role reports to the research editor, and you’ll work closely together to lead ProPublica’s seven-member research team, which works collaboratively across our national, regional and Local Reporting Network desks.

As Deputy Research Editor, You Will: 

  • Alongside the research editor, manage research reporters as they work on investigative stories. You’ll directly supervise reporters on the team.
  • Serve as an escalation point for research reporters and newsroom staff, helping resolve complex reporting challenges, tight deadlines and sensitive sourcing or verification issues.

  • Help build and maintain strong relationships with editors, reporters, partner newsrooms and other specialty teams at ProPublica, ensuring research is integrated early and effectively into reporting.
  • Contribute to hiring, onboarding, mentoring and giving performance feedback for a distributed research staff.
  • Assist with management and administration of, and help inform contract negotiations for, research tools and resources used by the newsroom, including evaluating new technologies, databases and applications relevant to investigative reporting.
  • Promote a collaborative, inclusive and supportive team culture that values rigor, curiosity and shared success.

  • In-depth knowledge of financial, corporate, government, legal or OSINT resources.
  • An understanding of the use of AI in investigative reporting.
  • Deep experience identifying, obtaining, searching and analyzing public records, with a strong understanding of government documents and processes at local, state and federal levels.
  • Expert ability to guide staffers in evaluating and vetting information from diverse sources, including proficiency in searching and using premium databases. 
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and quickly use emerging technologies and applications relevant to investigative research.
  • Experience building morale and fostering professional growth in a geographically distributed team.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with an appetite for working across the newsroom and with external partners.

  • Exceptional organizational, analytical and problem-solving skills, with a proven ability to manage multiple projects, meet tight deadlines and perform effectively under pressure. 
  • Willingness and ability to travel occasionally for staff retreats, training or other required events.

We are open to remote candidates, but those able to work from our New York or D.C. offices are strongly encouraged. Applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S.

title: Digital & Social Platform Editor

We are building Semafor to enable world-class journalists to deliver reporting and insights with rigor in journalistic forms that ensure a new level of transparency. Want to join us? Read on. 

About the Role

Semafor is seeking a Digital & Social Platform Editor to help amplify our journalism across platforms and formats.

This is not a  traditional “social posting” role. We’re looking for someone who understands how modern media travels — across video, live events, podcasts, breaking news, YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, X, and emerging platforms. The right candidate understands that packaging and distribution is editorial — and an important part of propelling our journalism forward.

This role sits at the center of newsroom, audience, video, audio, and events. You’ll help shape the strategy for how Semafor’s journalism is framed, edited, clipped, promoted, and distributed in real time . 

You should have strong editorial instincts, comfort with video and light editing workflows, sharp news and platform judgment, and a deep understanding of how to create platform-native content that drives reach without compromising editorial quality. Interest in business, politics, media, technology, and global affairs is important.

Responsibilities

Packaging & Distribution of Our Best Journalism

  • Work with newsroom leaders to identify the strongest moments, angles, and formats for distribution across scoops, breaking news, enterprise reporting, interviews, video, podcasts, and live journalism

  • Publish and optimize content across LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and emerging platforms

  • Knowledge of analytics, audience development, and platform performance trends
  • Interest in business, politics, media, technology, and global affairs
  • Work closely with video and audio producers to extend the reach and lifecycle of original content
  • Execute social video editing, formatting, subtitling, and platform optimization
  • Ability to clip, package, and publish short-form video from interviews, podcasts, newsroom shoots, and live events

Events & Promotion

  • Support promotional campaigns for Semafor events, franchises, and editorial launches

  • Help extend the reach of Semafor’s live journalism before, during, and after events
  • Develop and implement promotion plans for shows and big events across all platforms

Audience & Editorial Collaboration

  • Partner closely with the newsroom and audience teams to identify distribution opportunities and audience growth strategies
  • Apply editorial judgment to determine what content should travel, where it should live, and how it should be framed
  • Monitor performance trends, audience behavior, and platform shifts to inform publishing strategy
  • Maintain Semafor’s editorial standards, voice, and accuracy across all distributed content

Qualifications

  • 3-5 years of experience in social media, audience development, digital publishing, or platform distribution
  • Strong editorial instincts and understanding of news judgment
  • Experience publishing across major social and video platforms, with a particular focus on LinkedIn, YouTube, X, and Reddit
  • Understanding of platform-native storytelling and audience behavior

description: Job Details JOB BAND: C CONTRACT TYPE: Permanent, Full-time DEPARTMENT: BBC News LOCATION: Ultimo, Sydney Any offer of employment with the BBC will be conditional upon you having the right to work in Australia. Interviews will be held in the week commencing 16 November. PURPOSE OF THE ROLE Journalists on the Digital News team in Sydney play a crucial role in delivering continuous coverage for the BBC’s digital audiences in the UK and globally. The team picks up from UK and US colleagues to drive major stories as they unfold, shaping output for audiences in North America, Asia and elsewhere, while meticulously preparing the UK morning offer seven days a week. Journalists work across stories, live pages and video to produce sharp coverage, help curate editions of the website and BBC News app, and collaborate with correspondents worldwide to bring trusted reporting to millions. This role is required to work across a seven-day roster. WHY JOIN THE TEAM The BBC News website is one of the world’s largest and most popular news sites, with mobile and desktop editions for the UK and international audiences, as well as US and Asia editions, plus UK-facing and international-facing apps. We recently expanded our digital news operation in Sydney, recruiting digital journalists to cover international and UK news in text and video. This operation performs a crucial role in building the global audiences coming to the BBC as well as setting up our digital coverage to best serve and help grow the early morning UK audience coming to the site. YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT: Produce high-quality news stories, live pages and digital video that cover major UK and global events for audiences of millions. Continue coverage handed over from London and Washington, ensuring seamless reporting before UK teams come online each morning. Deliver accurate, engaging journalism, from breaking news to features, with strong editorial judgement, flair and context. Create a range of digital outputs, including short video edits, clips for other platforms, and curated live updates. Monitor social, search and audience data to inform storytelling, while maintaining a strong grasp of UK and international news agendas. YOUR SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE ESSENTIAL CRITERIA: Strong experience of writing accurate, engaging and fast-paced news in text for digital audiences. Experience in producing and editing short news video clips or a sharp understanding of what makes for compelling news video. Experience of covering the UK and the international news agenda in text and video and a familiarity with the BBC’s editorial values. Familiarity with using social media, search and audience data to improve storytelling and broaden coverage. The ability to come up with angles and approaches to the big stories of the day that will help us reach new and diverse audiences.
